page: Amazon Web Services c9g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server equipped with 192 dedicated ARM64 vCPUs built on AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 192 physical cores with one thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 96 MB L3 cache. System memory comprises 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, delivering a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Baseline network connectivity is rated at 100 Gbps. The instance provides no local storage drives and includes zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and parallel processing. The server achieves top-decile scores in stress-ng multi-threaded tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, software compilation using Clang, and bzip3 decompression. In-memory and network serving metrics show strong capabilities, recording 520.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 351.23 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Both cached and uncached DDR5 memory access speeds perform in the top 10 percent, while single-core CPU metrics and LLM text generation speeds yield average to poor relative results.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high core density create a compute-heavy profile suitable for multi-threaded, memory-bandwidth-sensitive workloads. Recommended deployment scenarios include large-scale software compilation pipelines, parallel compute clusters, high-concurrency static web serving, and distributed in-memory key-value data stores.
